bullets.title: Fed's Waller turns hawkish: rate hikes in December and March now baseline
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller has pivoted decisively from his dovish-insurance stance to favoring a modest hiking cycle, citing Core PCE stuck between 2.5–3.0% since spring 2024 with 'not sufficient progress' toward 2%. Three new shocks underpin the view: war-driven commodity prices, AI buildout passing through to consumer prices, and potential new trade conflicts. Waller sees the short-run neutral rate moving higher and is not concerned that tighter policy threatens a damaging slowdown.

bullets.title: GS argues current 3.0% Core PCE is mostly transitory; sees 2.2% by end-2027
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs attributes ~three-fourths of the 0.7pp Core PCE overshoot to mismeasurement or one-time factors: AI-related consumer electronics mispricing (0.3pp), jet fuel passthrough via airfares (0.2pp), energy cost passthrough (0.3pp), and tariff effects (0.1pp). GS expects gradual disinflation to 2.2% Core PCE by December 2027, pushes second rate hike to December, and sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes further hikes are unnecessary — directly at odds with Waller's hawkish read.

bullets.title: Oil surges 4.5% on Strait of Hormuz attacks; Pentagon preparing Iran strike options
bullets.body: WTI crude rallied to ~$92/bbl (+4.5%) and Brent to ~$104/bbl (+4.2%) on Strait of Hormuz attacks and reports of US CENTCOM completing Iran strike preparations. VLCC tanker rates surged to ~$1.4M/day, roughly 6x pre-war levels. Hurricane Isaias separately shut in ~511K bpd of Gulf production. The combination is pressuring broad equity markets and reinforcing the hawkish inflation narrative.

bullets.title: 10-year yield breaks above 5.33–5.34%; rate-sensitive stocks under pressure
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield has broken above its 5.33% multi-year support level to 5.34%, per technician Craig Johnson, pressuring interest-sensitive sectors. Hedgeye flags UST 10yr immediate-term range of 5.15–5.38% and maintains bond shorts; global yields are at higher cycle highs. Higher borrowing costs are also being cited in real estate (Citi REIT daily) as compressing REIT valuations and reducing fiscal headroom.

bullets.title: S&P 500 tape: 72% of stocks declining, Russell 2000 at new cycle lows (-9% from peak)
bullets.body: Despite major indices near record highs, market internals are deteriorating sharply: only 27% of tracked stocks are in uptrend (Craig Johnson), 72% of S&P 500 names fell an average of 1.4% on Wednesday (Hedgeye), and the Russell 2000 is down 9% from its cycle peak making new lows. VIX remains below 19. SPX immediate-term support is 7,688–7,853. Small caps are underperforming NDX amid rate backup and weak breadth.

bullets.title: Labor market stays historically tight: initial claims 197k for 4th straight week below 200k
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell 2k w/w to 197k, marking the fourth consecutive week below 200k, with the 4-week average at 198k. The 13-week smoothed series is down 11.8% y/y. Continuing claims ticked up 17k to 1,716k but remain at cycle lows. The data reinforces the 'labor market is stable' component of Waller's hawkish pivot.

bullets.title: MS September CPI preview: headline 3.7% y/y, core eases to 0.24% m/m
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley forecasts September headline CPI at +0.62% m/m / +3.7% y/y — elevated primarily due to energy — while core CPI eases to 0.24% m/m (2.5% y/y) from 0.29% in August, driven by wireless fee normalization. Core goods inflation remains positive and airfares/health services partially offset the decline in wireless. The print will be a key near-term catalyst for rate expectations.

bullets.title: META Muse is reshaping sector risk premia: telcos -15-25%, AI agent disruption broadening
bullets.body: Meta's Muse agentic AI product — now #1 in the US App Store for 21 consecutive days with 2M+ DAUs — has been upgraded to negotiate directly with telecom, utility, and insurance providers on users' behalf. US telco/utility/insurance stocks have declined 15–25% on bill-negotiation fears. Morgan Stanley flags Muse as 'the most credible agentic threat to commerce and advertising to date.' 22V Research argues consumer AI agents lower switching costs and represent a structural margin risk to financial services and retail.

bullets.title: TSMC September revenue +54.6% y/y; Samsung profits up ~9x — AI demand keeps chipmakers in hypergrowth
bullets.body: TSMC reported September revenue growth of ~55% y/y on strong AI chip demand, while Samsung's 3Q operating profit rose nearly ninefold on memory prices and HBM shipments. Despite these prints, semi stocks are under broad pressure in the session (SOXX -1.65% premarket, multiple names -2-4%) — suggesting the bar is extremely high and macro headwinds (yields, oil) are overriding beat dynamics.

bullets.title: ORCL/AVGO pursuing $40-50B+ debt financings for AI chips; hyperscale capex arms race escalates
bullets.body: Oracle is seeking ~$40B in financing via a special-purpose entity to lease NVDA chips, while Broadcom is arranging $50B+ financing for OpenAI custom AI chip buildout (with Apollo/Blackstone as lenders). Amazon has guided to ~$220B in 2026 capex and purchase of 2M NVDA GPUs. AWS CEO sees data center supply constraints in power, memory, and networking persisting. This is the clearest signal yet that AI infrastructure spending is entering a new, larger phase.

bullets.title: Data center moratoriums spreading; $200B+ in US projects face cancellation from regulatory opposition
bullets.body: San Francisco, Oakland, and Raleigh have approved data center moratoriums; Austin is proposing new water-usage regulations. Duke Energy's settlement requires major tech load customers to fund infrastructure and pay 75% of projected monthly power. Over $200B in US data center projects face cancellation. Separately, the Dodge Momentum Index's data center planning component decelerated for a second straight month (-1.3% M/M commercial in September).

bullets.title: Trump suspends MSFT, ADBE, and major IT outsourcers from H-1B PERM green card program
bullets.body: VP Vance and Labor Secretary Sonderling suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant, Tata Consultancy Services, and Capgemini from the Permanent Labor Certification Program, citing multiple active federal investigations and alleged H-1B system abuse. IT consulting stocks moved to session lows on the announcement. Stocks were flat on the day initially but the action represents a meaningful escalation of immigration enforcement targeting the tech sector's talent pipeline.

bullets.title: 3Q26 earnings season setup: large-cap EPS revised up to $354 from $313; tech/comm services leading margins
bullets.body: S&P 500 full-year 2026 EPS estimates have risen to $354 from $313 at the start of the year, with upward revisions across all market caps since late August despite the Fed hiking cycle. Technology and Communication Services are driving large-cap margin leadership. Small caps recorded the largest upward revisions but guidance quality is deteriorating — share of companies lowering guidance has risen since 2Q, particularly among small caps. Technology sector forecast to lead Q3 with 88%+ positive surprises.

bullets.title: China Golden Week: polarized consumers, services strong, high-end goods weak
bullets.body: Domestic travel volumes were broadly flat (+0.6% y/y, 2.1bn trips) but mix shifted value: camping up 410% vs. May Day, tier-3 city flights up 30%+. Macau footfall rose ~20% y/y but premium mass and VIP fell double digits, implying GGR down mid-to-high single digits. Movie box office collapsed to Rmb1.14bn vs. Rmb2.1bn in 2024. Goods consumption was polarized: household appliances +40%, mobile +120%, but catering only +3–7% and Hainan duty-free spending per shopper weakened despite traffic gains.

bullets.title: UK fiscal position deteriorating: £65bn additional consolidation still needed by 2030
bullets.body: JPMorgan estimates UK still needs ~£65bn (1.8% of GDP) in medium-term fiscal consolidation beyond mapped plans, with the 10-year gilt yield at 5.3% and trend growth revised down to 1.1% offsetting recent tightening. Fiscal headroom under existing rules has declined from £23.6bn to ~£12bn. Hidden spending pressures of £20–25bn (defense to 3% of GDP, potential austerity reversal) are unbudgeted. The October Budget is expected to be fiscally neutral with only ~£5bn in tax increases.

bullets.title: Hedgeye/22V positioning: short IWM/Russell, short duration, long energy/crypto; non-AI cyclicals not yet a re-short
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains shorts in Russell 2000 (down 9% from peak, making new cycle lows), utilities, European equities, and duration (TLT), while adding to Brent crude long and initiating Ethereum/Solana positions. 22V Research advises against pressing shorts in non-AI cyclicals (banks, retailers, industrials) in the near term given improved risk/reward after recent drawdown — preferring to wait for post-earnings entry. Hard-asset HALO cyclicals are preferred over AI-agent-exposed financials and retailers.

bullets.title: GOOGL Gemini Agent Enterprise launch positions against OpenAI; Unity Spark adds game-creation distribution muscle
bullets.body: Google announced Gemini Agent for enterprise with model flexibility (Claude, open models), competing directly with OpenAI's corporate offerings. Separately, Google and Unity launched Unity Spark, an AI-powered game creation platform distributed via Google's ecosystem, posing a competitive threat to Roblox and Meta's Horizon. Morgan Stanley estimates 1M Unity Spark users could add ~$14.9M EBITDA to Unity (~1.2% of 2028 estimates). Roblox is seen maintaining its social-layer moat with 123M+ DAUs.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure/power stocks hit 3rd-percentile positioning; OPCO sees oversold entry
bullets.body: Oppenheimer notes power/AI infrastructure positioning has reset to the 3rd percentile with valuations normalized per Goldman Sachs. The firm is bullish into earnings on GEV, AMSC, ORA, MOD, and OUST as positioning resets. The sector lagged since mid-August on bear flattening, rising 2-year yields, diesel prices, and data center moratorium political risk — but OPCO argues these headwinds are reflected in current valuations.

bullets.title: Crypto positioning escalating: IBIT up 13 spots in 1-week ETF rankings; Hedgeye adds ETH and SOL
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Keith McCullough bought 100bps of IBIT (Bitcoin ETF) and 50bps of SOLZ (Solana ETF) while initiating an Ethereum position, making crypto his third-largest position cluster behind Bitcoin. IBIT ranked #6 overall in his macro ETF rankings, up 13 spots in one week and 20 spots over one month. ETHA (Ethereum ETF) ranked #8, up 12 spots in a week. The crypto bid is occurring alongside — not instead of — the broader risk-off in equities.

bullets.title: Waymo raises private debt to $5B; Uber acquires ezCater for $2.3B in catering expansion
bullets.body: Waymo upsized its private debt raise to $5B (from $3B) at 5.25% over benchmark, funded by Blackstone, Sixth Street, and PIMCO, with a fleet of 4,000+ vehicles and IONIQ 5 scaling to 30K annual capacity starting 2028. Uber countered offensively by acquiring ezCater for $2.3B in cash — 140K+ restaurants, $2.5B TTM gross bookings, high-teens YoY growth — expanding Uber Eats into high-AOV catering. The Waymo deal increases competitive overhang on Uber's core rideshare business while the ezCater deal is described as margin-accretive at an assumed 18% take rate.
